courses.course_name: Bachelor of Management Accounting
courses.course_description:
The Bachelor of Science in Management Accounting (BSMA) is a degree program focused on the use of accounting and financial information to support internal business management and decision-making. Students learn how to prepare, analyze, and interpret financial and operational information that can help organizations plan, control operations, manage costs, evaluate performance, and make informed business decisions.
The program covers management accounting, financial accounting, cost accounting, budgeting, financial analysis, taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, and other business-related areas. Unlike programs focused primarily on external financial reporting and public accountancy, management accounting emphasizes the use of accounting information for planning, internal decision-making, performance evaluation, and organizational management .
career_paths: Other accounting, finance, and business-related positions

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting Technology
courses.course_description:
The Bachelor of Science in Accounting Technology (BSAcT) is a degree program focused on the application of accounting principles, financial processes, and accounting technology in business and organizational settings. Students learn how to record, process, analyze, and report financial information using accounting principles and computerized accounting systems.
The program combines accounting knowledge with the practical use of technology in business operations. It prepares students to work with financial records, accounting systems, financial reports, taxation, auditing-related processes, internal controls, and other accounting and business functions.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Engineering
courses.course_description:
The Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Engineering is a professional engineering degree program that prepares students for careers involving the design, analysis, development, manufacturing, operation, maintenance, and improvement of aircraft and related aeronautical systems.
The program develops a strong foundation in mathematics, physics, basic engineering sciences, and aeronautical engineering principles. Students study areas related to aircraft structures, aerodynamics, propulsion, aircraft systems, aircraft design, maintenance, and other technologies used in the aviation industry.
The program prepares students to contribute to the technological and socioeconomic development of the aviation industry, particularly in areas such as aircraft research, development, manufacturing, maintenance, operation, and aviation education. The profession is regulated in the Philippines, and aeronautical engineering practice includes professional services involving aircraft structures, power plants, accessories, and related engineering activities.
obtainable_skills: Aircraft propulsion and power plant fundamentals

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Agri-Biosystems Engineering
courses.course_description:
Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering is a specialized engineering discipline that applies engineering science and design to the processes and systems involved in the sustainable production, post-production, and processing of safe food, feed, fiber, timber, and other agricultural and biological materials. It also covers the efficient utilization, conservation, and management of natural and renewable resources to enhance human health in harmony with the environment .
The program integrates engineering principles with biological, environmental, and agricultural sciences, allowing students to develop competencies in specialized areas such as agricultural machinery and power, land and water resources, structures and environment, and bioprocess engineering. Students learn to design systems and solve complex problems related to agriculture, food production, and natural resource management, addressing challenges in food security, energy, and environmental sustainability .
obtainable_skills: Application of knowledge of mathematics and science to solve complex agricultural and biosystems engineering problems
Design and conduct of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data
Functioning effectively in multidisciplinary and multi-cultural teams
Identification, formulation, and solution of complex engineering problems
Understanding of professional and ethical responsibility
Effective communication of complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large
Understanding of the impact of engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context
Recognition of the need for, and engagement in, life-long learning
Use of modern engineering tools, techniques, and software necessary for ABE practice
Knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles for project management
Understanding of at least one specialized field of ABE practice
career_paths: National Government Agencies (e.g., DA, DOST, DENR, BSWM)
NGOs focused on sustainable farming and food systems

sources.title: CMO No. 94, series of 2017
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: Focuses on foundational sciences and mathematics essential for all engineering disciplines. This includes General Chemistry, Calculus I and II, Physics for Engineers, and introductory agricultural sciences such as Principles of Crop Science and Principles of Animal Science. General education courses are also taken to develop communication and critical thinking skills. Students are introduced to the field through an introductory course in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students delve deeper into engineering sciences and core principles. The curriculum typically covers Engineering Mechanics (Statics and Dynamics), Differential Equations, Engineering Data Analysis, Computer-Aided Drafting, and Principles of Soil Science. These subjects provide the fundamental principles of mechanics, mathematics, and soil science that are crucial for agricultural and biosystems applications.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students transition to specialized ABE core subjects, learning the application of engineering principles to biological and agricultural systems. The curriculum covers topics such as AB Machinery and Power Engineering, AB Structures and Environment, AB Land and Water Resources Engineering, AB Process Engineering, and Engineering Economy. This year is intensive in theory and application, providing the specific technical knowledge required of an agricultural and biosystems engineer.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: This final year emphasizes integration, application, and professional practice. Students typically take advanced courses in their chosen specialization and work on a capstone design project where they apply their cumulative knowledge to a significant agricultural and biosystems engineering problem. An internship/practicum is required to provide industry experience. Students are also expected to take the Fundamentals of Engineering examination, which is the first step to becoming a licensed professional engineer.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness
courses.course_description:
Agribusiness is a specialized field that focuses on creating and going into business in agriculture. It is a systems-oriented discipline emphasizing the interactions of all activities and factors affecting the manufacture and distribution of farm supplies; production activities on the farm; and the storage, processing, and distribution of farm commodities and items made from them, locally and globally, within the context of the country's biophysical, socio-cultural, political, and economic environment and development needs.
The program integrates business management principles with agricultural production and marketing, aiming to produce professionals capable of managing and growing sustainable agribusinesses, taking into consideration all value chain activities affecting the agricultural sector. Students learn to analyze agricultural markets, develop business plans, manage financial resources, and understand the economic and policy environment affecting the agricultural sector, ultimately preparing them to be technically and managerially competent agribusiness managers and/or entrepreneurs.
obtainable_skills: Communication skills and strategies, both verbal and non-verbal
Entrepreneurial attitudes, skills, and professional work ethics
Ethical, collaborative intra- and interpersonal relations
Diagnosis and analysis of agribusiness opportunities and threats
Formulation and implementation of systems-oriented strategic plans
Monitoring and evaluation of agribusiness programs
Leadership and advocacy for agribusiness policies
Environmental protection and sustainable development advocacy

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students focus on foundational courses in business, economics, and the natural sciences. This typically includes Principles of Management, Basic Accounting, General Mathematics, and introductory courses in agriculture and economics. General education courses are also taken to develop communication and critical thinking skills. The first year establishes the core knowledge base in business and agriculture.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students delve deeper into business and economic principles, including Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Business Finance, and Marketing Principles. They may also take more specialized courses in agricultural production and technology. The curriculum begins to integrate business concepts with agricultural applications, preparing students for more specialized agribusiness courses.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students transition to specialized agribusiness subjects, focusing on the application of business principles to the agricultural sector. This may include courses in Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Marketing, Cooperatives and Rural Development, and Agribusiness Policy. Students learn to manage agribusiness enterprises, develop marketing strategies, and analyze policy issues affecting the agricultural sector.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: This final year emphasizes integration and application. Students typically take advanced agribusiness courses, such as Strategic Agribusiness Management and Agribusiness Enterprise Development. A capstone project, business plan, or thesis is often required. An internship/practicum may also be required to provide industry experience. The year culminates in a comprehensive understanding of the agribusiness field.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Biology
courses.course_description:
Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 49, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Science in Biology program is structured as a generalized framework for biological study. Its primary purpose is to ground students in the fundamental concepts, principles, and theories of the biological sciences and to introduce them to the conduct of biological research. The program moves beyond the common perception of being solely a pre-medical track and aims to produce professional biologists.
The study of biology encompasses a wide range of specializations, from the traditional fields like botany, zoology, and microbiology to modern areas such as molecular biology, biotechnology, and genomics. The curriculum provides a balanced treatment of all major branches of biology, ensuring students gain a comprehensive understanding of life from the molecular to the ecosystem level. Students learn to apply biological knowledge to address real-world problems, including those related to health, food security, and environmental sustainability.

Employment in government agencies (e.g., Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Department of Agriculture)
Employment in museums, zoos, and aquaria
NGOs for advocacy and communication work involving science, technology, and the environment
Writing science articles for newspapers, magazines, and books
Production of educational software or multimedia applications
Collection, preservation, and sale of biological specimens
Preparation for medical and other health-related graduate programs

Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 90, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Science in Ceramics Engineering (also referred to as Ceramic Engineering) program is designed to produce graduates who can apply engineering principles to the processing, production, and utilization of ceramic materials. The program covers the fundamental science and engineering of ceramics, including the structure, properties, processing, and applications of ceramic materials.
Ceramics Engineering deals with inorganic, non-metallic materials. Students learn about the extraction and processing of raw materials, the design and operation of furnaces and kilns, and the development of ceramic products for various industries, including construction, electronics, aerospace, and biomedical applications. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical skills in materials characterization, process optimization, and quality control.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering

Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 91, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program is designed to produce graduates who can apply the principles of chemistry, physics, mathematics, and engineering to design, develop, and operate processes and equipment for the production of chemicals, fuels, materials, and other products. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical skills through laboratory work, design projects, and industrial training. Graduates are prepared for careers in various industries, including petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, food processing, energy, and environmental management.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
courses.course_description:
Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 47, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Science in Chemistry program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in the fundamental principles and practices of chemistry. The program covers the five core disciplines of chemistry: inorganic, organic, analytical, physical, and biochemistry.
The BS Chemistry program is structured to produce graduates who can apply chemical principles to solve problems in various fields, including industry, research, and education. Students develop a strong foundation in chemical theory, laboratory skills, and analytical techniques. The curriculum includes extensive laboratory work, research projects, and professional exposure to prepare graduates for careers as professional chemists or for advanced studies in chemistry and related fields. The program also prepares students for the Chemistry Licensure Examinations.

Ability to recognize and implement accurate and precise scientific measurements
Computational and data processing skills relating to chemical information and data
Skills required in good laboratory practices including safety, waste management, and record keeping
Proper use of modern chemical instrumentation
Skills required for the conduct of standard laboratory procedures in analytical and synthetic work
Ability to design experiments and understand the limitations of the experimental approach
Communication skills, covering both written and oral communication
Numeracy and calculation skills, including error analysis and correct use of units
Ability to use computers as information and research tools
Interpersonal skills relating to the ability to interact with other people and to work in a team
Study and self-development skills needed for continuing professional development and life-long learning
Ability to exercise ethical principles and social responsibility

The curriculum covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, mathematical economics, and various specialized fields such as development economics, international economics, and public finance. Students develop skills in economic analysis, quantitative methods, and policy evaluation. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and the application of economic principles to real-world issues. Graduates are prepared for careers in government, banking, finance, research, and the private sector, as well as for advanced studies in economics and related fields.
obtainable_skills: Economic Analysis: Ability to analyze economic issues using economic theories and models.
Quantitative Methods: Proficiency in econometrics, statistics, and mathematical economics.
Policy Evaluation: Skills in evaluating economic policies and their impacts.
Research Skills: Competence in conducting economic research and data analysis.
Critical Thinking: Ability to think critically and solve complex economic problems.
Communication Skills: Effective written and oral communication of economic concepts and findings.
Economic Literacy: Understanding of microeconomics, macroeconomics, and various economic fields.
Ethical and Professional Conduct: Adherence to ethical standards and professional responsibility in economic practice.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
courses.course_description: Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 88, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program is designed to produce graduates who can apply engineering principles to the design, development, and maintenance of electrical systems and equipment. The program covers the generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy. The curriculum covers fundamental areas such as circuits, electronics, electromagnetics, power systems, control systems, and electrical machines. Students learn to analyze, design, and implement electrical systems, considering factors such as safety, efficiency, and sustainability. The program emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical skills through laboratory work, design projects, and industrial training. Graduates are prepared for careers in various industries, including power generation, manufacturing, telecommunications, and research.

Power Systems: Understanding of power generation, transmission, distribution, and protection.
Control Systems: Skills in designing and implementing control systems for electrical applications.
Communication and Teamwork: Effective communication and collaboration skills for working in multidisciplinary teams.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education
courses.course_description: Based on the official CHED PSG (CMO No. 74, s. 2017), the Bachelor of Elementary Education program is designed to prepare students for teaching in the elementary level (Grades 1-6). The program equips students with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to effectively teach various subjects to young learners. The curriculum covers general education, professional education (pedagogical courses), and a specialization component. Students learn about child development, teaching methodologies, curriculum development, assessment, and classroom management specific to the elementary level. The program emphasizes the integration of theory and practice through field study and student teaching. Graduates are prepared to become effective elementary school teachers who can foster the holistic development of children.
obtainable_skills: Teaching Skills: Ability to plan, implement, and evaluate effective instruction for elementary students.
Classroom Management: Skills in managing elementary classrooms and creating a positive learning environment.
Child Development: Understanding of child development and its application to teaching practices.
Research Skills: Ability to conduct action research and contribute to educational scholarship.
Ethical and Professional Conduct: Adherence to professional ethics and standards of the teaching profession.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science (BS ES) is a four-year interdisciplinary undergraduate program that prepares students to understand environmental systems and address environmental problems through scientific investigation and sustainable resource management. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in History
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Arts in History (BA History) is a four-year humanities program that develops students' systematic understanding of the human past through the study, interpretation, analysis, and evaluation of historical events, societies, cultures, institutions, and historical evidence. The program trains students to critically examine primary and secondary sources, reconstruct and interpret historical developments, conduct historical research, and communicate evidence-based interpretations of the past. It also develops an understanding of Philippine, Asian, and world history and the relationships between historical events and broader social, political, economic, and cultural developments. History is therefore not limited to memorizing dates and events. The discipline involves research, source criticism, contextual analysis, interpretation, argumentation, and historical writing, enabling graduates to apply historical thinking in education, research, government, cultural institutions, media, heritage, and other fields.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Industrial Technology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Industrial Technology (BIndTech) is an undergraduate technology program focused on developing practical, technical, and industry-oriented competencies for the application of technology in industrial and related work environments. The program combines foundational academic learning with specialized technical and practical training. Students develop the ability to operate and work with technological equipment, apply technical procedures, troubleshoot problems, perform measurements and testing, maintain equipment, and apply appropriate technologies in production and service environments. The program may be offered through different technology specializations, so the specific technical competencies students acquire depend on their chosen major. CHED-recognized program inventories, for example, show BIndTech offerings with majors such as Automotive Technology, Civil Construction Technology, Electrical Technology, Electronics Technology, Mechanical Technology, and Refrigeration & Airconditioning Technology.
obtainable_skills: Operation of industrial equipment and tools
career_paths: Technical Trainer/Instructor, subject to applicable qualifications

The program prepares students to identify organizational and user requirements, select and integrate appropriate computing technologies, develop and administer computer-based solutions, and maintain IT environments. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Interior Design
courses.course_description: Interior Design is the art and science of planning, specifying, selecting, and organizing interior spaces, including surface finishes, materials, furniture, furnishings, fixtures, and other interior elements. The discipline focuses on creating interior environments that appropriately respond to their intended function, movement, character, users, and surrounding built environment. The program develops students' ability to identify and solve interior design problems, formulate design concepts and strategies, integrate design theories and philosophies, and communicate design proposals through visual, oral, written, and digital/virtual methods. It also incorporates knowledge of art and design history, period styles, materials, furniture, building construction, utilities, color, legislation, technology, and professional practice.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Landscape Architecture
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (BLA) is a professional undergraduate program focused on the study, planning, design, development, and management of outdoor environments for human use and enjoyment. The field combines design, environmental science, ecology, natural and social sciences, landscape technology, and engineering concepts to create functional, aesthetically appropriate, sustainable, and environmentally responsive outdoor spaces. Students learn to analyze sites and landscapes, develop design solutions, communicate designs graphically and verbally, and manage the implementation and evaluation of landscape projects. The program also emphasizes ecology, conservation, preservation, sustainable development, professional practice, legal and ethical responsibilities, and the relationship between people and their physical environment. Landscape architecture is also a regulated profession in the Philippines under Republic Act No. 9053, which defines its professional scope to include planning, designing, supervising, and administering the development of natural scenery and outdoor spaces, as well as environmental protection, conservation, and rehabilitation.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year establishes the foundational knowledge and practical skills essential for a maritime career. Students are introduced to the maritime profession through courses on Ships, Ship Routines and Ship Construction and Navigational Instruments with Compasses. They begin developing their technical proficiency in Terrestrial and Coastal Navigation and understanding basic ship stability principles with Trim, Stability, and Stress. Foundational general education courses are also taken to build communication, mathematical, and scientific skills.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year builds on the fundamentals with more specialized and advanced maritime topics. Students deepen their navigation skills with courses in Celestial Navigation and Terrestrial and Coastal Navigation 2. They learn the rules of the sea through Collision Regulations, start exploring cargo operations with Cargo Handling and Stowage, and are introduced to ship management with Leadership and Teamwork. Practical skills are further developed with courses on Meteorology and Oceanography and Maritime Communications, which includes GMDSS training. 3RD YEAR (SHIPBOARD TRAINING) The third year consists of a mandatory one-year Onboard Training (OBT) as a seagoing service, which is a requirement for the conferment of the degree. During this period, students complete a Training Record Book (TRB) to document the practical application of their knowledge and skills under the supervision of qualified officers. This is the culminating phase where they gain real-world experience as part of a ship's crew, preparing them for their roles as officers. Students must perform bridge watchkeeping duties under the supervision of the master or a qualified officer for a period of not less than six (6) months. 4TH YEAR (PROFESSIONAL STAGE) The final academic year is the professional stage. It is at this stage where the graduating students are equipped with additional knowledge and skills required for their roles as officers, such as Third Mates. This year focuses on integrating prior knowledge with advanced professional courses like Voyage Planning, Operational Use of RADAR/ARPA, Operational Use of ECDIS, Ship Handling and Maneuvering, and Maritime Law. This stage develops the sense of responsibility and decision-making capabilities expected of a maritime officer.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Materials Engineering (BS MatE)
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Engineering is an engineering discipline dedicated to the study of materials and their behavior, focusing on the interconnection between composition, structure, processing, and properties. It equips students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to design, develop, and optimize materials such as metals, polymers, ceramics, semiconductors, and composites for targeted applications across various industries.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics essential for engineering. Students take courses in General Chemistry, Physics, and Calculus to develop their analytical skills. They are also introduced to the engineering profession through an introductory course in Materials Engineering and fundamental engineering sciences like Engineering Graphics and Statics of Rigid Bodies.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year deepens the understanding of core engineering and materials science principles. Students explore the structure-property relationships of materials and learn about rate processes that govern material behavior. Courses in Strength of Materials, Dynamics of Rigid Bodies, Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, and Mathematical Methods in Engineering are taken to build a comprehensive engineering toolkit.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on the advanced core of the Materials Engineering discipline. Students delve into Materials Analysis and Testing, Materials Synthesis and Processing, and Materials Fabrication. They learn to apply their knowledge through laboratory work and are introduced to Computer Applications, Systems Evaluation, and Experimental Designs for engineering problem-solving and research. An internship (On-the-Job Training) is often completed during this period to provide valuable industry experience.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, integrating all prior learning. Students apply their skills to Materials Selection and Design and more specialized topics like Degradation of Materials and Forensic Engineering. They take a thesis or capstone project course to conduct independent research and develop innovative solutions. Students take courses on Laws and Ethics for Materials Engineers and professional electives.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics (BS Math)
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematics is an undergraduate program that provides students with a deep and broad understanding of mathematics as both a theoretical discipline and a practical tool. Mathematics is described as the science of patterns, where mathematicians seek to discover, analyze, and classify patterns in abstract objects and natural phenomena. The program covers traditional domains such as quantity (arithmetic), structure (algebra), space (geometry), and change (analysis). The program emphasizes distinctive mathematical modes of thought including abstraction, generalization, deduction, inference, use of symbols, and the axiomatic method.
obtainable_skills: Rigorous Argument and Proof: Construct and evaluate formal mathematical proofs and logical arguments.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in basic mathematical concepts and skills. Students begin with the Calculus sequence (Calculus I and II) and are introduced to the fundamentals of computing. General Education courses are taken to develop communication and critical thinking skills. Students are also introduced to the fundamental concepts of mathematics, which serves as a bridge to more advanced abstract thinking.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year deepens the understanding of core mathematical principles. Students complete the Calculus sequence (Calculus III) and take Abstract Algebra I and Linear Algebra to explore algebraic structures. They are introduced to Probability and begin studying Advanced Calculus, which forms the foundation for mathematical analysis. Courses in General Physics and other non-math foundational courses provide exposure to the application of mathematics in other fields.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced core areas of mathematics. Students take courses in Differential Equations, Modern Geometry, and an advanced course in analysis or algebra. They explore topics such as Complex Analysis, Statistical Theory, and either Numerical Analysis or Mathematical Modeling. Students begin selecting mathematics electives to explore areas of interest, preparing them for more specialized study.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, integrating all prior learning through a Thesis or Special Problem course. Students take additional mathematics electives and qualified electives/cognates to develop a specialization or research focus. Advanced topics such as Topology or Elementary Number Theory are covered. This year culminates in the completion of a research paper that organizes and presents a body of mathematics in a detailed, coherent, and original manner.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Statistics (BS Stat)
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Statistics is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students for careers as statisticians and data scientists. Statistics is the science and art of uncertainty, with roots from biology and mathematics. Its role is to characterize and understand the random process that leads to uncertainty, equipping one with tools that facilitate decision-making. Statistics aggregates data into meaningful information that is used in decision-making.
obtainable_skills: Statistical Theory: Demonstrate broad and coherent knowledge in core areas of statistics.
Data Analysis: Apply appropriate statistical tests and methods for given problems.
Statistical Computing: Use computing technologies and statistical software for data analysis.
Data Generation: Conceptualize strategies for generating timely and accurate/reliable data.
Problem-Solving: Translate real-life problems into statistical problems.
Decision-Making: Select optimal solutions to problems and make decisions in the face of uncertainty.
Research: Design and implement research studies and experiments.
Communication: Communicate results of statistical analysis to stakeholders and decision-makers.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a foundation in mathematics, computing, and general education. Students take courses in Descriptive Statistics, Reasoning of Mathematics, and Basic Programming Language. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to statistical concepts and data analysis.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core statistical and mathematical concepts. Students take courses in Mathematical Statistics 1, 2, and 3, covering probability, distributions, and statistical inference. They learn about Linear Algebra and Matrix Theory, Calculus II and III, and Statistical Software. Students develop skills in statistical computing and data analysis.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced statistical methods and applications. Students take courses in Regression Analysis, Experimental Designs, Survey Sampling, and Survey Operations. They learn about Nonparametric Statistics and Bayesian Statistics. Students begin selecting statistics, mathematics, and computing electives.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through advanced courses and a thesis or special project. Students take courses in Time Series Analysis, Multivariate Analysis, and Categorical Data Analysis. They complete a thesis or special problem that demonstrates their ability to apply statistical methods to real-world problems.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts major in Biology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Biology (BS Biology) is a four-year program that provides students with a comprehensive understanding of biological concepts, theories, and principles. The program develops skills in scientific methods and processes, as well as competence in the use of laboratory, technological, and computer equipment for scientific inquiry pursuits. Students acquire biological concepts that broaden their view of their own being and of their environment. The program recognizes that learning is a life-long and self-motivated process due to the continuous unraveling of facts and principles. Students show strong appreciation and valuing of life and interrelatedness of living things in the ecosystem. They pursue solutions to personal, environmental, and other societal problems and develop desirable traits of inquisitiveness, perseverance, accuracy, creativity, and cooperation. The program is a preparatory program for those aspiring to enter the fields of biomedical research, biotechnology, human medicine, and other allied health professions.
obtainable_skills: Depth and breadth of knowledge of fundamental biological concepts
Nationalism by advocating the protection and preservation of Philippine flora and fauna species

courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (BSCE) is a four-year engineering program that prepares students to plan, design, construct, operate, and maintain infrastructure and civil works. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
courses.course_description: Industrial Engineering is an engineering discipline concerned with designing, improving, and managing integrated systems involving people, materials, information, equipment, energy, and processes. The program prepares students to analyze how work and production systems operate and to improve their efficiency, productivity, quality, safety, cost-effectiveness, and overall performance. Students apply mathematics, engineering principles, statistics, operations research, systems analysis, human factors, and management concepts to solve problems in manufacturing, services, logistics, healthcare, business, and other organizational environments. Unlike engineering disciplines focused primarily on designing a particular physical structure or machine, Industrial Engineering focuses on optimizing systems and processes as a whole.

sources.title: CHED Memorandum Order No. 96, Series of 2017; CMO No. 86, Series of 2017
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in basic sciences, mathematics, and general engineering principles. Students take courses in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, and Engineering Drawing. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to the engineering profession and basic computer applications.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core engineering sciences and industrial engineering fundamentals. Students study Statics of Rigid Bodies, Dynamics of Rigid Bodies, Strength of Materials, and Engineering Materials. They learn about Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, and Electrical Circuits. Laboratory courses provide hands-on experience with basic engineering systems.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on core industrial engineering subjects. Students take courses in Operations Research, Production Planning and Control, Quality Control, and Supply Chain Management. They learn about Facilities Planning and Design, Ergonomics, and Engineering Economics. Laboratory courses and design projects provide practical application of theoretical concepts.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through capstone design projects and professional courses. Students complete a major design project that demonstrates their ability to apply industrial engineering principles to solve real-world problems. They take courses on Professional Ethics, Laws and Contracts, and Engineering Management. An internship or on-the-job training may also be required to provide industry experience.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering With Specialization in Hydraulics and Water Resources Engineering
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (BSCE) is a four-year engineering program that prepares students to plan, design, construct, operate, and maintain infrastructure and civil works . It applies mathematics, physical sciences, engineering mechanics, materials science, and engineering design to the development of safe and functional infrastructure. A Hydraulics and Water Resources Engineering specialization focuses on the planning, design, operation, and management of water resources systems including water supply, irrigation, drainage, flood control, hydrology, and water quality management . Students develop competencies in hydraulic engineering, hydrology, water resources planning, irrigation and drainage design, flood mitigation, and sustainable water management .

Students take courses in calculus, physics, chemistry, and introductory engineering subjects. General education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to civil engineering concepts and professional practice.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces fundamental engineering sciences and basic civil engineering subjects. Students take courses in mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials science, and surveying. They learn about structural analysis and engineering mathematics. Computer- aided design and engineering visualization skills are developed.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on core civil engineering and water resources engineering specialization courses. Students take advanced courses in hydrology, hydraulics, water supply systems, and irrigation engineering. They also study environmental engineering and water quality management. Engineering economics and project management courses are taken. Laboratory work and field studies provide practical experience.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, culminating in comprehensive engineering courses, research projects, and practicum experiences. Students undertake a civil engineering design project or thesis related to water resources engineering. They complete on-the-job training or internship in engineering firms or government agencies. Students take professional engineering practice courses.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in basic sciences, mathematics, and general engineering principles. Students take courses in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, and Engineering Drawing. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to programming and basic engineering concepts.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core engineering disciplines and robotics fundamentals. Students study Statics of Rigid Bodies, Dynamics of Rigid Bodies, Strength of Materials, and Engineering Materials. They learn about Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, and Computer Programming. Laboratory courses provide hands-on experience with basic systems.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on core robotics subjects. Students take courses in Kinematics and Dynamics of Robotic Systems, Control Systems, Sensors and Actuators, and Embedded Systems. They learn about Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence. Laboratory courses and design projects provide practical application of theoretical concepts.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through capstone design projects and professional courses. Students complete a major design project that demonstrates their ability to apply robotics engineering principles to solve real-world problems. They take courses on Professional Ethics, Laws and Contracts, and Engineering Management. An internship or on-the-job training may also be required to provide industry experience.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Elementary Education major in General
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) is a four-year teacher education program designed to prepare students to teach learners at the elementary level. The program develops both pedagogical knowledge and multidisciplinary content knowledge needed to teach the major learning areas encountered in elementary education. The General/Generalist track provides broad preparation rather than limiting students to a single subject specialization. Students develop competencies in learner development, teaching strategies, curriculum planning, assessment, classroom management, inclusive education, educational technology, and elementary-level content areas such as language, mathematics, science, social studies, and values education.

sources.title: CMO No. 74, Series of 2017 - Policies, Standards and Guidelines for Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd). The supplied CMO No. 52, Series of 2007 is older and has been superseded.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Geodetic Engineering major in Land Surveying
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Geodetic Engineering (BSGE) is a four-year engineering program that prepares students to measure, analyze, and manage accurate spatial information about the Earth's surface and physical features. The program combines mathematics, physical sciences, surveying, geodesy, mapping, positioning technologies, photogrammetry, remote sensing, and geographic information systems. The land surveying component focuses particularly on determining and establishing the location, dimensions, boundaries, elevations, and physical characteristics of land through surveying measurements, field observations, computations, mapping, and geospatial technologies.

sources.title: The primary PSG for the base degree is CMO No. 89, Series of 2017 (Policies, Standards and Guidelines for the Bachelor of Science in Geodetic Engineering (BSGE) Program). The "major in Land Surveying" is not a CHED-recognized major in the applicable BSGE PSG.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Geological Engineering
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Geological Engineering is an engineering program that applies geological knowledge, engineering principles, mathematics, and physical sciences to problems involving the Earth's materials, geological structures, natural resources, and geologic hazards. Students study the properties and behavior of rocks, minerals, soils, and geological formations and learn how geological conditions affect engineering projects and resource development. The field is particularly relevant to mineral and energy exploration, mining, construction, infrastructure development, groundwater assessment, slope stability, geohazard evaluation, and environmental management.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering major in Geotechnical
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (BSCE) is a four-year engineering program that prepares students to plan, design, construct, operate, and maintain infrastructure and civil works. It applies mathematics, physical sciences, engineering mechanics, materials science, and engineering design to the development of safe and functional structures and infrastructure. The Geotechnical specialization focuses on the engineering behavior of soil, rock, and subsurface materials and how these materials interact with structures and infrastructure. Students develop knowledge applicable to foundations, earth structures, excavation, retaining systems, slope stability, site investigation, and other engineering projects where subsurface conditions are critical to safety and performance.
obtainable_skills: Apply knowledge of mathematics and science to solve complex civil engineering problems
Design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data
Design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints, in accordance with standards
Function in multidisciplinary and multi-cultural teams
Identify, formulate, and solve complex civil engineering problems
Communicate effectively civil engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large
Understand the impact of civil engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context
Recognize the need for, and engage in life-long learning
Use techniques, skills, and modern engineering tools necessary for civil engineering practice
Understand at least one specialized field of civil engineering practice

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Graphics and Design (BSGD)
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Graphics and Design (BSGD) is an undergraduate program focused on the creative, technical, and professional application of visual communication and design. It develops students' ability to transform concepts and information into effective visual outputs using traditional and digital media. The program is aligned with the broader Fine Arts and Design field described by CHED, which emphasizes aesthetic concerns, visual communication, creative use of media and technologies, design principles, and the production of artworks and design products. Graphic design specifically involves organizing visual elements to communicate intended messages to identified audiences. Students develop competencies in graphic design, visual communication, typography, illustration, digital design, layout, image creation and editing, design research, and portfolio development.
career_paths: Based on the Fine Arts and Design PSG (CMO No. 43, s. 2017):

sources.title: The primary regulatory reference is CMO No. 43, Series of 2017 (Policies, Standards and Guidelines (PSGs) for the Undergraduate Programs in Fine Arts and Design). The submitted course title is not an exact degree title prescribed in CMO No. 43, s. 2017. The CMO directly covers the Graphics and Design field, particularly Graphic Design under Visual Communication, and establishes the educational standards, outcomes, curriculum framework, and professional directions applicable to Fine Arts and Design programs. However, the exact degree title "Bachelor of Science in Graphics and Design" is not the degree name directly prescribed in CMO No. 43. The CMO's prescribed degree framework uses Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) and Bachelor in various Arts and Design, with specializations including Graphic Design.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology major in Heating, Ventilating and Airconditioning-Refrigeration Engineering Technology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Engineering Technology (BET) is an applied engineering technology program that combines engineering principles with practical technical knowledge, laboratory work, equipment operation, technology application, and problem-solving. Unlike traditional engineering programs that emphasize theoretical engineering design and analysis, engineering technology programs generally place greater emphasis on applying engineering concepts to technical and industrial systems. For an HVAC-R Engineering Technology specialization, the field focuses on heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration systems. Related HVAC-R engineering technology education typically involves thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid flow, refrigeration cycles, electrical systems and controls, equipment selection, system installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, energy efficiency, and building environmental systems.

sources.title: CMO No. 86, Series of 2017 is directly applicable to Bachelor of Engineering Technology (BET) programs because its scope expressly covers requirements common to Bachelor of Science in Engineering and Bachelor of Engineering Technology programs. However, it is not a discipline-specific PSG for HVAC-R Engineering Technology. It establishes common requirements rather than the detailed curriculum and program standards for this particular specialization.

courses.course_description: The Home Economics field is concerned with the application of knowledge and skills related to family and household resource management, food and nutrition, clothing and textiles, human development, housing and living environments, consumer education, and livelihood or enterprise development. Home Economics education combines practical and applied knowledge with principles from areas such as nutrition, family resource management, clothing and textiles, food preparation, human development, and community or livelihood development. However, because the exact Bachelor of Science in Home Economics title was not sufficiently verified as the current CHED program title, this description should be treated as a field-level description, rather than a definitive description of a current BS Home Economics curriculum.
career_paths: Based on the Home Economics field:

sources.title: The submitted CMO No. 44, Series of 1997 is directly relevant to the Home Economics academic field and is an old CHED policy/standards document for Home Economics education. However, the available official CHED program inventories reviewed show Home Economics primarily appearing as a major/specialization under teacher-education programs, such as Bachelor of Technology and Livelihood Education – Home Economics, rather than clearly establishing Bachelor of Science in Home Economics as a current standardized CHED degree title.
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a foundation in general education and introductory food and service management concepts. Students take courses in Food Preparation, Basic Nutrition, and Introduction to Hospitality Management. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to the teaching profession and learn about child and adolescent development. Early field study experiences provide initial exposure to the school environment.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core food and service management and pedagogical skills. Students take courses in Food Science, Menu Planning, and Food Safety and Sanitation. They learn about Baking and Pastry Arts. Professional education courses in principles of teaching, assessment of learning, and educational technology are taken. Field study courses continue, allowing students to observe and participate in classroom activities.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced food and service management topics and teaching methodologies. Students take courses in Advanced Food Preparation, Hospitality Management, and Entrepreneurship. They learn about curriculum development and educational research. More advanced field study experiences enable students to design and implement learning activities under supervision.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, culminating in practice teaching (internship) and a comprehensive review. Students undertake full-time student teaching in cooperating schools or technical-vocational institutions, applying all their acquired knowledge and skills under the guidance of a cooperating teacher and a supervising instructor. They complete a research project or action research related to food and service management education. Students take courses on the professionalization of teaching and ethical responsibilities.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences
courses.course_description:
Based on the official Ateneo de Manila University program description:
The Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences is an honors degree that can be completed within four years. The program of study is seamlessly designed for future health professionals and physicians aspiring to continue their training in medical education, particularly at the Ateneo School of Medicine and Public Health. The Core Curriculum provides a foundation for using the multi-disciplinary approach in the study of health while relevant course offerings in Social Sciences and Management further deepen this approach. The courses have been meticulously arranged in a sequential manner to enable the students to acquire the knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values necessary for them to become outstanding healthcare professionals, dynamic leaders, and decisive social catalysts .
obtainable_skills: Knowledge of health systems and management
Social sciences and management applications in health
Preparation for medical education and health professions
career_paths: Based on the official Ateneo de Manila University program description :
Physician / Medical Professional (with further medical education)

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Human Services
courses.course_description:
Based on CMO No. 33, s. 2017:
The Bachelor in Human Services (BHumServ) is an undergraduate social-science and helping-professions program that prepares students to provide basic human-services assistance in educational institutions, communities, and organizations. The program focuses on understanding individuals, groups, organizations, communities, and their interactions; identifying conditions that affect human functioning; and developing appropriate assistance, referral, advocacy, intervention, and support activities. Students also develop professional helping skills, ethical values, client-centered attitudes, program planning, evaluation, and research competencies. The program prepares graduates for entry-level human-services roles such as human services personnel/assistant, intervention design assistant, and training assistant, with applications in educational institutions, communities, and industry .
obtainable_skills: Understanding of human development and functioning
Understanding of individual, group, organizational, and community systems

sources.title: CMO No. 33, Series of 2017 – Policies, Standards and Guidelines for the Bachelor in Human Services (BHumServ) Program. The official CHED title is "Bachelor in Human Services (BHumServ)" without "of Science" .
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students establish foundations in general education and introductory Human Services concepts. Important areas include human development and functioning, human services and mental health, self-development and client awareness, communication, and foundational social-science knowledge.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students develop core helping-profession competencies through areas such as general psychology, basic statistics, skills for helping professionals, human-services delivery systems and interventions, group processes and facilitation, psychological assessment, and understanding exceptionalities and special populations.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students progress toward more advanced professional applications. Key areas include communication for Human Services professionals, program development and evaluation, human-services interventions, mental-health and psychosocial support in emergency settings, values and ethics in helping professions, research methods, and specialized cognates. Students may also develop competencies related to children and adolescents, needs assessment, career development, community services, social development, and other allied fields depending on the institution's curriculum.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students integrate their knowledge through field experience in industry, schools, or communities, research, thesis work, advanced electives/cognates, and other culminating requirements.

courses.course_name: Bachelor in Industrial Design
courses.course_description:
Based on CMO No. 43, s. 2017:
Industrial Design under the Fine Arts and Design framework is a design discipline focused on developing products and objects that balance aesthetic qualities, functional use, and production feasibility. Students learn to transform concepts into product designs through visual communication, design principles, drawing, materials exploration, model-making, design research, and design development. The program combines creative and technical design thinking to address the appearance, usability, materials, construction, and production considerations of products. CMO No. 43, s. 2017 identifies Industrial Design/Product Design within its Fine Arts and Design specializations and specifies that graduates in Industrial Product Design should be proficient in applying art and design principles to develop designs for aesthetic appreciation, functional use, and production feasibility .
career_paths: Based on the Fine Arts and Design PSG (CMO No. 43, s. 2017):

sources.title: CMO No. 43, Series of 2017 – Policies, Standards and Guidelines (PSGs) for the Undergraduate Programs in Fine Arts and Design. The CMO states that the degree programs covered include Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) and Bachelor in various Arts and Design, with Industrial Design included among the design specializations. The sample curriculum specifically identifies "Bachelor of Fine Arts (Industrial Design)" .
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students establish foundations in art, design, drawing, visual communication, design principles, creativity, and general education. The emphasis is on developing fundamental visual and creative skills while introducing students to the principles and processes used in design.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students develop stronger technical and design competencies through areas such as design drawing, materials, form development, digital design tools, product visualization, model making, and introductory industrial/product design. Students begin applying design principles to practical product and user-related problems.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students move into more advanced industrial design practice. They work on product concepts, design research, user requirements, materials and production processes, computer-aided design, prototyping, and product development. Projects become more complex and require students to integrate aesthetic, functional, technical, economic, and user considerations.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students integrate their design and technical competencies through advanced industrial design projects, professional practice, research, internship or related experiential learning, and a culminating design project or thesis/capstone requirement depending on the institution's approved curriculum.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Technology major in Industrial Design Technology
courses.course_description: Industrial Design Technology under an Industrial Technology program combines practical technology training with product and industrial design. The program develops technical competencies for designing, developing, producing, and improving products while considering functionality, materials, manufacturing processes, aesthetics, and user requirements. Unlike a Bachelor of Fine Arts specialization in Industrial Design, the Industrial Technology pathway places stronger emphasis on technical and applied industrial competencies. Students develop practical skills related to design development, materials, production techniques, drafting, fabrication, prototyping, and the operation or application of technologies used in industrial production. Official university records confirm that Industrial Design Technology is offered as a major under Bachelor of Science in Industrial Technology.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Instrumentation and Control Engineering
courses.course_description: Instrumentation and Control Engineering is an engineering discipline concerned with the measurement, monitoring, automation, and control of engineering systems, industrial equipment, machinery, and processes. The field combines engineering principles with measurement systems, sensors, signal processing, control systems, automation, instrumentation, electronics, and related technologies. Instrumentation and control engineers design, develop, install, operate, maintain, and improve systems used to measure process variables and automatically regulate industrial and engineering processes. An official curriculum from Batangas State University describes the program as preparing students to become instrumentation and control specialists responsible for designing, developing, installing, managing, and maintaining equipment and systems used to monitor and control engineering systems, machinery, and processes.
obtainable_skills: Troubleshooting of instrumentation and control systems
Programming and use of engineering software/tools

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students establish the mathematical, scientific, and engineering foundation required for later instrumentation and control courses. Important areas include calculus, physics, chemistry, programming, engineering drawing, and introductory engineering concepts. The emphasis is on developing quantitative reasoning, scientific analysis, laboratory skills, and fundamental engineering problem-solving.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students progress into core engineering sciences and electrical/electronic concepts. They begin developing stronger knowledge of circuits, electronics, measurement principles, engineering mathematics, and fundamental instrumentation concepts. Laboratory activities become increasingly important as students learn to apply theoretical engineering concepts to physical systems and measurements.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students move into the specialized areas of instrumentation and control engineering. Important areas may include instrumentation systems, sensors and transducers, measurement systems, control theory, process control, signal processing, industrial automation, and related engineering applications. Students increasingly learn how to design, analyze, integrate, test, and troubleshoot measurement and control systems.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: Students apply their specialized engineering knowledge to more complex industrial and engineering problems. Advanced instrumentation, automation, control applications, engineering management, professional practice, and related areas are developed. The final stage commonly includes industrial training/internship and a culminating design, research, or project component, depending on the institution's curriculum. Batangas State University's curriculum, for example, includes professional preparation and practical application within its BSICE program.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering major in Land and Water Resources Engineering
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (BSABE) is an engineering degree that applies engineering science and design to agricultural, biological, environmental, and natural-resource systems. The Land and Water Resources Engineering specialization focuses on the engineering planning, development, conservation, and management of land and water resources. Important applications include irrigation and drainage, soil and water conservation, land development, hydrology/agrometeorology, water-resource systems, dams, farm roads and bridges, and related agricultural and environmental infrastructure. The program combines engineering mathematics and sciences with agricultural and biological sciences, engineering design, resource management, and practical applications. Official university program descriptions identify land development, irrigation and drainage, soil and water resources, environmental management, and related infrastructure as major areas of BSABE practice. The specialization is also directly represented in the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering profession. Republic Act No. 10915 identifies Land and Water Resources Engineering as one of the competency areas covered by the Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering licensure examination.

sources.title: CMO No. 94, Series of 2017 – Policies, Standards and Guidelines for the Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (BSABE) Program Effective Academic Year (AY) 2018-2019. The supplied CMO No. 86, s. 2017 establishes requirements common to BS Engineering degrees and Bachelor of Engineering Technology programs. It is therefore applicable to BS engineering programs generally, but it is not the specific PSG for BS Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering. The course-specific issuance is CMO No. 94, Series of 2017 .
sources.used_for: Course description, obtainable skills, and career paths

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a foundation in mathematics, physical sciences, and basic engineering principles. Students take courses in calculus, physics, chemistry, and introductory engineering subjects. General education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to civil engineering concepts and professional practice.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces fundamental engineering sciences and basic civil engineering subjects. Students take courses in mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials science, and surveying. They learn about structural analysis and engineering mathematics. Computer- aided design and engineering visualization skills are developed.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on core civil engineering and water resources engineering specialization courses. Students take advanced courses in hydrology, hydraulics, water supply systems, and irrigation engineering. They also study environmental engineering and water quality management. Engineering economics and project management courses are taken. Laboratory work and field studies provide practical experience.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, culminating in comprehensive engineering courses, research projects, and practicum experiences. Students undertake a civil engineering design project or thesis related to water resources engineering. They complete on-the-job training or internship in engineering firms or government agencies. Students take professional engineering practice courses.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year establishes the foundational knowledge and practical skills essential for a maritime career. Students are introduced to the maritime profession through courses on Ships, Ship Routines and Ship Construction and Navigational Instruments with Compasses. They begin developing their technical proficiency in Terrestrial and Coastal Navigation and understanding basic ship stability principles with Trim, Stability, and Stress. Foundational general education courses are also taken to build communication, mathematical, and scientific skills.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year builds on the fundamentals with more specialized and advanced maritime topics. Students deepen their navigation skills with courses in Celestial Navigation and Terrestrial and Coastal Navigation 2. They learn the rules of the sea through Collision Regulations, start exploring cargo operations with Cargo Handling and Stowage, and are introduced to ship management with Leadership and Teamwork. Practical skills are further developed with courses on Meteorology and Oceanography and Maritime Communications, which includes GMDSS training. 3RD YEAR (SHIPBOARD TRAINING) The third year consists of a mandatory one-year Onboard Training (OBT) as a seagoing service, which is a requirement for the conferment of the degree. During this period, students complete a Training Record Book (TRB) to document the practical application of their knowledge and skills under the supervision of qualified officers. This is the culminating phase where they gain real-world experience as part of a ship's crew, preparing them for their roles as officers. Students must perform bridge watchkeeping duties under the supervision of the master or a qualified officer for a period of not less than six (6) months. 4TH YEAR (PROFESSIONAL STAGE) The final academic year is the professional stage. year_levels.overview: The first year establishes the foundational knowledge and practical skills essential for a maritime career. year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR

Students must perform bridge watchkeeping duties under the supervision of the master or a qualified officer for a period of not less than six (6) months. 4TH YEAR (PROFESSIONAL STAGE) The final academic year is the professional stage. It is at this stage where the graduating students are equipped with additional knowledge and skills required for their roles as officers, such as Third Mates. This year focuses on integrating prior knowledge with advanced professional courses like Voyage Planning, Operational Use of RADAR/ARPA, Operational Use of ECDIS, Ship Handling and Maneuvering, and Maritime Law. year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics essential for materials science. Students take courses in General Chemistry, Physics, and Calculus to develop their analytical skills. They are also introduced to fundamental engineering principles such as Engineering Graphics and Statics of Rigid Bodies.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year deepens the understanding of core scientific and engineering principles. Students study Structure-Property Relationships of Materials, Thermodynamics of Materials, Strength of Materials, and Dynamics of Rigid Bodies. Laboratory courses provide hands-on experience in materials characterization and testing.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on the advanced core of the Materials Science and Engineering discipline. Students delve into Materials Analysis and Testing, Materials Synthesis and Processing, and Materials Fabrication. They learn to apply their knowledge through laboratory work and are introduced to Computer Applications, Systems Evaluation, and Experimental Designs for engineering problem-solving and research. An internship (On-the-job Training) is often completed during this period to provide valuable industry experience.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The fourth year integrates prior learning through advanced courses and the beginning of research work. Students study Degradation of Materials, Materials Selection and Design, and Forensic Engineering in Materials. They may also take professional electives in specialized areas such as nanomaterials, biomaterials, or electronic materials.

year_levels.label: 5TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is dedicated to the capstone of the program. Students focus on their research thesis or capstone project, conducting independent research to develop innovative solutions. They also take courses on Laws and Ethics for Materials Engineers.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in basic mathematical concepts and skills. Students begin with the Calculus sequence (Calculus I and II) and are introduced to the fundamentals of computing. General Education courses are taken to develop communication and critical thinking skills. Students are also introduced to the fundamental concepts of mathematics, which serves as a bridge to more advanced abstract thinking.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year deepens the understanding of core mathematical principles. Students complete the Calculus sequence (Calculus III) and take Abstract Algebra I and Linear Algebra to explore algebraic structures. They are introduced to Probability and begin studying Advanced Calculus, which forms the foundation for mathematical analysis. Courses in General Physics and other non-math foundational courses provide exposure to the application of mathematics in other fields.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced core areas of mathematics. Students take courses in Differential Equations, Modern Geometry, and an advanced course in analysis or algebra. They explore topics such as Complex Analysis, Statistical Theory, and either Numerical Analysis or Mathematical Modeling. Students begin selecting mathematics electives to explore areas of interest, preparing them for more specialized study.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, integrating all prior learning through a Thesis or Special Problem course. Students take additional mathematics electives and qualified electives/cognates to develop a specialization or research focus. Advanced topics such as Topology or Elementary Number Theory are covered. This year culminates in the completion of a research paper that organizes and presents a body of mathematics in a detailed, coherent, and original manner.

They are introduced to basic industrial safety and shop practices. General Education courses develop critical thinking and communication skills.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core mechanical and industrial technology concepts. Students learn about engineering materials, strength of materials, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics. They begin developing skills in technical drawing and CAD. Courses in manufacturing processes and machine shop practice provide hands-on experience.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced technical and managerial topics. Students study machine design, industrial automation, quality control, and industrial management. They learn about maintenance engineering and reliability. Laboratory courses provide practical experience with industrial equipment and processes. Students may also complete an internship or on-the-job training in an industrial setting.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through capstone projects and specialized courses. Students take advanced courses in areas such as robotics, mechatronics, or energy systems. They complete a capstone project that demonstrates their ability to apply technical knowledge to solve real-world industrial problems. Students take courses on industrial safety, environmental management, and entrepreneurship.
