year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a strong foundation in basic sciences, mathematics, and general engineering principles. Students take courses in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, and Engineering Drawing. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to the engineering profession and basic computer-aided design.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core engineering sciences. Students study Statics of Rigid Bodies, Dynamics of Rigid Bodies, Strength of Materials, and Engineering Materials. They learn about Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, and Electrical Circuits. Laboratory courses provide hands-on experience with basic mechanical systems and testing equipment.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced core subjects and specialization areas. Students take courses in Machine Design, Heat Transfer, Internal Combustion Engines, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, and Power Plant Engineering. They learn about Manufacturing Processes and Industrial Management. Design projects and laboratory work provide practical application of theoretical concepts.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through capstone design projects and professional courses. Students complete a major design project that demonstrates their ability to apply engineering principles to solve real-world problems. They take courses on Professional Ethics, Laws and Contracts, and Engineering Economics. An internship or On-the-job training may also be required to provide industry experience.

courses.course_description: CMO No. 35, Series of 2005 provides the Minimum Policies and Standards for Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science (BS ES). The BS ES program is closely allied to the biological sciences, earth sciences, and physical sciences, and relates to mathematics, particularly in modeling and statistics. The Natural Resource Management major is a specialization within the BS ES program that focuses on the sustainable management of natural resources. year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR

year_levels.label: 5TH YEAR

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR

Students take advanced courses in areas such as power plant management, energy economics, and environmental compliance. year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year deepens the understanding of English and pedagogical skills. Students take courses in Philippine Literature, World Literature, and Linguistics. year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced English topics and teaching methodologies. Students take courses in Literary Criticism, Creative Writing, and English for Specific Purposes. Students begin selecting English electives to deepen their content knowledge.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, culminating in practice teaching (internship) and a comprehensive review. Students undertake full-time student teaching in cooperating schools, applying all their acquired knowledge and skills under the guidance of a cooperating teacher and a supervising instructor. They complete a research project or thesis related to English education. Students take courses on the professionalization of teaching and ethical responsibilities. Advanced English topics such as Stylistics, Discourse Analysis, or Translation Studies may also be offered.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a foundation in general education and introductory security concepts. Students take courses in Fundamentals of Industrial Security, Human Rights Education, and Introduction to Philippine Criminal Justice System. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Students are introduced to personnel security and human resource management.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core security disciplines. Students take courses in Information Security, Physical Security Systems, and Introduction to Security Administration and Management. They learn about Fundamentals of Investigations and Intelligence, Professional Conduct and Ethical Standards, and Introduction to Management and Leadership. Students begin developing skills in statistics and research.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced security topics and practical applications. Students take courses in Introduction to Cyber Crime, Executive Protection Management, Criminal Law, and Evidence. They learn about Corporate and Security Investigation, Emergency Planning and Disaster Management, Security of Critical Infrastructures, and Asset Protection Management. Students begin selecting electives and preparing for practicum.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year integrates all prior learning through practicum and specialized courses. Students take courses in Crisis Management and Business Continuity Plan, Business and Competitive Intelligence, Crime Prevention, Detection and Control, and Crime Scene Protection and Preservation. Students complete a 540-hour practicum divided into two components: Practicum 1 in Government Agencies and Practicum 2 in Private Institutions.

year_levels.label: 1ST YEAR
year_levels.overview: The first year builds a foundation in general education and introductory special needs education concepts. Students take courses in Adolescent Development, Foundations of Special Needs Education, and Introduction to Inclusive Education. General Education courses develop communication, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills. Early field study experiences provide initial exposure to special education settings.

year_levels.label: 2ND YEAR
year_levels.overview: The second year introduces core special needs education concepts and pedagogical skills. Students take courses in Educational Psychology, Learning Theories, and Assessment in Special Needs Education. They learn about Curriculum Development and Instructional Strategies. Professional education courses in principles of teaching and assessment of learning are taken. Field study courses continue, allowing students to observe and participate in special education classrooms.

year_levels.label: 3RD YEAR
year_levels.overview: The third year focuses on advanced special needs education topics and teaching methodologies. Students take courses in Behavior Management, Teaching Learners with Specific Disabilities, and Transition Planning. They learn about Vocational Education and Community-Based Instruction for secondary learners. More advanced field study experiences enable students to design and implement learning activities for learners with special needs.

year_levels.label: 4TH YEAR
year_levels.overview: The final year is the capstone of the program, culminating in practice teaching (internship) and a comprehensive review. Students undertake full-time student teaching in special education settings at the secondary level, applying all their acquired knowledge and skills under the guidance of a cooperating teacher and a supervising instructor. They complete a research project or action research related to special needs education. Students take courses on the professionalization of teaching and ethical responsibilities.

research_sequence: Established schema and salary-evidence hierarchy before course mapping.
Validated one representative course from each of the 13 canonical clusters.
Applied the same controlled occupation catalog and mapping rules to all 342 courses.
Ran structural, preservation, salary, source, year, and confidence validations after export.

methodology.salary_estimation: All salaries are estimates in gross Philippine pesos per month. Exact occupation pages retain their published low/high range but are rounded to the nearest practical band. PSA occupation means are converted to intentionally broad rounded ranges. Niche roles without occupation-level evidence use cluster/industry proxy bands and are marked low confidence.
methodology.mapping_policy: Direct titles receive high confidence. Specializations mapped to a close broader occupation receive medium confidence and an explicit mapping note. Roles supported only by an industry proxy receive low confidence.
methodology.scope: Philippine employment only; ranges combine early-to-mid-career market variation and are not guaranteed starting salaries.
